items.title: EchoFG: display timing (the generated frame's present blocks 17-20 ms): vsync / VRR / frame latency
items.note: 2026-10-11 retest (x3 at about 30 fps, 4K 120 Hz, GPU scaling on): the FSR path's generated-frame Present takes 16.7-18.4 ms, EchoFG's 6.4-6.9 ms: the long wait was FSR's. With EchoFG the display shows two presents inside one refresh in about 19% of cases (refresh gaps 0:157 1:460 2:200; FSR path 0:~2) and the presenting thread comes back only 1.6 ms before the next real frame (FSR path 6-7 ms): 90 presents a second on a 120 Hz screen with little slack. Open: is VRR really on (Sync mode Default = interval 0, no tearing flag?), and the slack. Owner, 2026-10-11: Lossless Scaling's Sync mode changed to Off (allow tearing): nothing visible changes; Sync mode stays as it was. (The log had no new session after it yet, so the refresh-gap line for that setting is not measured.) BUILT 2026-10-11 (deployed to D: next): presents are put one to a refresh of the display (setting 'Put the presents one to a refresh of the display', on by default; from DXGI frame statistics; switches itself off on a variable refresh). The log says 'the presents are put one to a refresh ... (a steady N Hz refresh)' or why not. Offline it can only show 'not steady' (this machine's G-Sync window), so whether it is active at the owner's, and whether the 0-gaps (19%) go away, is for the live log: `dev.py logs` prints the per-engine gap shares. Audit of the presenter after that (2026-10-11): (1) the display statistics were never reset for a new swap chain, so a counter that restarted read as '4294967278 presents not seen' in the log (fixed: they start again with each swap chain, device or backwards count); (2) the refresh alignment's slot memory could drift into the future after a restart and pile all the presents at the end of the interval (fixed: forgotten after 100 ms, and it steps aside when the presents of one real frame cannot fit the refreshes, e.g. x7 at 30 fps on 120 Hz); (3) its 'steady' test took ~13 stretches to settle (fixed: 2).

items.title: Neural Rendering: Model preset (newer or older model) in the panel and settings
items.note: 2026-10-19. NVIDIA's runtime 310.9.16 (nvngx_dlssnr.dll cdfa6c1e..., compat-fp16, supplied by the owner) runs a newer, smaller model by default (DLSSNR.Hint.Render.Preset 0/2) and keeps the older one as preset 1 (the only model in 310.8). Offline on the 4070 Ti SUPER: one run 3.2/6.0/9.1/19.6 ms (older, 540p/1080p/1440p/4K) against 2.0/3.5/5.3/10.9 (newer), about 1.7x; the older model inside the new DLL gives the same output and cost as the 310.8 file (mean change 31.50 of 255 at 720p; the newer 20.43, an effect about like 0.7 pass). Setting 'modelPreset' 0..2 (panel: Newer / Older), read when the model is made (the model is rebuilt on a change), not part of a look. Host test passes (SDR, scRGB, PQ, no NaN, highlights kept). Research: github.com/GrimsVerk/nr-runtime-research (310.9.16 preset parameter and values). Deployed to D:\Utilities\Lossless Scaling 2026-10-19 (old model file kept in backups\).

items.title: FSR 4 runtime on NVIDIA driver 617.42: the host scenario fsr_runtime_switch stalls on the first picture and the host dies at exit (0xC0000005 in nvwgf2umx.dll)
items.note: 2026-10-19, full matrix (72 scenarios, 615 s, 3 at a time) with the new model: everything passes except fsr_runtime_switch, which fails the same way alone (2 of 2): the switch to the FSR 4 runtime (external/fsr4/amd_fidelityfx_dx12.dll) never finishes a frame ('the engine had finished 0 of 2 frames', 235 of 237 pictures not handed over), then at shutdown the host faults in nvwgf2umx.dll+0x4493f0 (null read, 0x2c) with the engine thread inside amd_fidelityfx_dx12 -> D3D12Core -> the driver. The default FSR 3.1 runtime scenarios pass. Machine: driver 617.42 (the last green matrix was on an older driver, 2026-10-09/11). Not seen live. To do: run the same switch live (FSR Upscaler, Runtimes list +); if it only stalls, the stall monitor stops the addon after 20 s as designed; check what exiting Lossless Scaling does with the engine thread stuck in the driver; try an older driver or the AMD-signed FSR 4 if available. Same family as S6.

items.title: The recorder as a feature of the manager, not of each addon (and a note when recording cannot work)
items.where: src/addon/recorder.{h,cpp}, runtime.cpp Record() and the tap; echofg_addon.cpp; manager Features tab
items.note: Owner's wish, 2026-10-19. Found the same day: the Neural Rendering addon records nothing when its own Enable is off (runtime.cpp: the dispatch and present callbacks return at once when !g_config.enabled, so Record() is never fed): the panel just says 'Waiting for frames'. Today the recorder lives in every addon (DLSS5NR01, the upscalers, EchoFG each feed it; the setting is mirrored into each addon's config since 0.9.18). Design to settle: (1) who finds the captured frame (the TAP: the largest colour texture among LS's recent passes, frame_tap.cpp) when no addon is on: it needs the manager's dispatch hook, which the addons use now; (2) one Recording section on the manager's Features tab (on, seconds, memory, folder, hotkey Ctrl+Shift+F1, Record what is shown) and a status line; (3) EchoFG's 'record a clip' and the OBS replay key stay the same key; (4) the .lsrec format and nr_lsrec do not change. Interim, small: in each addon's Recording section, say 'Recording needs this addon switched on (its Enable)' when the recorder is on and the addon is off.
